one_liner: Artificial Societies builds a foundation model to simulate human behavior for decision-making; its YC listing warrants a look, but reported funding puts it past HTGF’s pre-first-round window.

top_signals.signal: Listed as part of a recent European Y Combinator cohort.
Reported a Kindred Capital-led pre-seed in March 2025 and a Point72 Ventures-led seed in May 2025; the funding summary cites $5.35 million raised.

Model score 76.7 of 100 (at the top of the reference cohort). Positive inputs include three known founders, a co-founder CTO, deep-tech and B2B classifications, YC participation, and a top-university flag. The separate technical-founder flag is not confirmed by the founder records.

team: James He is co-founder and CEO, with the University of Cambridge listed. Patrick Sharpe is co-founder and CPO, with prior experience at iptiQ. Tom Whittle is listed as co-founder and CTO; the role does not independently verify his technical background.
why_early: Unknown whether either round was priced. The reported pre-seed and seed mean the company is already past its first funding round.
devils_advocate_risks: It is unknown how accurately the simulations predict real-world behavior.
Use of anonymized social media and transaction data may raise privacy and regulatory concerns.
next_step: HTGF Industrial Tech team: deprioritize for pre-first-round outreach. If meeting the founders, ask: What results have you seen when comparing model predictions with observed behavior on decisions the model had not seen before?
